titleTh: ขอเจ้าของห้องให้คนอื่นมาเช่าช่วง
scenarioSentences: You rent a room from Mr. Moretti.
You will study abroad for three months.
You don't want to pay for an empty room.
Your friend's cousin needs somewhere to live.
You call your landlord to ask.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Moretti, I'm studying abroad from January to March. Could someone use my room while I'm away?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Moretti
dialogue.text: You mean sublet it? Your contract doesn't usually allow that.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Otherwise, I'd be paying for an empty room for three months.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Moretti
dialogue.text: Who would it be? I'm responsible if anything goes wrong.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: My friend's cousin. She's a nursing student, quiet, and doesn't smoke.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Moretti
dialogue.text: I'd need to meet her first, and you'd still be responsible for the rent.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fine. She'd pay me, and I'd pay you as usual.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Moretti
dialogue.text: As long as I meet her and she signs an agreement, she can stay.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. Could she come by on Saturday morning?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Moretti
dialogue.text: Saturday at ten is fine.

titleEn: Questioning a mistake on a restaurant bill
titleTh: แจ้งร้านอาหารว่าบิลคิดเงินผิด
scenarioSentences: You had dinner with three friends at a restaurant.
The bill seems much higher than expected.
Two dishes appear on it twice.
Mr. Silva is the manager tonight.
You ask to speak with him.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Excuse me, Mr. Silva. I think there's a mistake on our bill.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Silva
dialogue.text: Sorry to hear that. What's the problem?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We ordered one fish curry and one lamb dish, but both are charged twice.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Silva
dialogue.text: Let me check. You're right, the order must have been entered twice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It added almost forty dollars. And to be honest, the food took ages to arrive.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Silva
dialogue.text: I apologize, we're short of staff tonight. I'll correct the bill, and desserts are on us.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's very kind. Could we see the new bill before we order dessert?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Silva
dialogue.text: Of course. I'll bring it with the dessert menu in a minute.

titleEn: Requesting time off for a family wedding
titleTh: ขอลางานไปงานแต่งญาติ
scenarioSentences: Your cousin's wedding is abroad next month.
You need five days off work to attend.
It is the shop's busiest month.
Ms. Wright, your manager, is strict about leave.
You ask her during your break.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Ms. Wright, could I have five days off next month? My cousin's getting married abroad.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Wright
dialogue.text: Next month? That's our busiest season. Five days would be very difficult.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I understand. What if I took three days and worked the weekend before?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Wright
dialogue.text: Three days is more reasonable. But who would cover your shifts?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Daniel said he might swap with me. He wants extra hours anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Wright
dialogue.text: If he agrees in writing, I can approve three days.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fair. I'll fly out on Thursday evening and be back for my Monday shift.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Wright
dialogue.text: Fine. Just get me his confirmation by Friday, otherwise I'll have to say no.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No problem. I'll talk to him today.

titleTh: คุยกับหัวหน้าเรื่องขอขึ้นเงินเดือน
scenarioSentences: You have worked at your company for two years.
Last year, you took on many new tasks.
Your pay has stayed the same.
Ms. Torres is your manager.
You have asked to meet her today.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks for meeting me. I'd like to talk about my salary.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Torres
dialogue.text: Of course. What's on your mind?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Since last year, I've trained new staff and managed two client accounts. My pay hasn't changed.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Torres
dialogue.text: That's true, and you've done it well. But the budget's tight until spring.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I understand, but I'd like my extra work to be recognized.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Torres
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I can start a pay review now. Any raise would begin in two months.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could I get an idea of how much?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Torres
dialogue.text: Around eight percent, as long as the review goes well. I'm confident it will.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That sounds reasonable. Could you confirm the timeline by email?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Torres
dialogue.text: Certainly. I'll send it this afternoon.

titleTh: วางแผนจัดปาร์ตี้ในซอยกับเพื่อนบ้าน
scenarioSentences: Your street is planning a summer party.
You and your neighbor Mrs. Kerr are organizing it.
You need permission to close the road.
Some older neighbors are worried about noise.
You meet to plan it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mrs. Kerr, the council needs our form by Friday. How long should we close the road?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Kerr
dialogue.text: I was thinking noon until ten at night.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's long. The Johnsons at number twelve are already worried about noise.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Kerr
dialogue.text: Hmm. What if we finished at eight instead?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's more reasonable. And starting at two gives people time to set up.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Kerr
dialogue.text: Fine, two until eight. We'll keep the music low after six too.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good. And food? A caterer would be expensive.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Kerr
dialogue.text: Let's ask every house to bring one dish to share. It's cheaper and more fun.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great idea. I'll put a note through every door this weekend.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Kerr
dialogue.text: And I'll send the form to the council tomorrow.

titleEn: Getting a refund for a canceled concert
titleTh: ขอเงินคืนค่าบัตรคอนเสิร์ตที่ถูกยกเลิก
scenarioSentences: You had two concert tickets for Saturday.
The singer is ill, so it's canceled.
You can't go on the new date.
Ms. Day works at the ticket office.
You ask her for a refund.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi. Saturday's concert was canceled. I'd like a refund for my two tickets.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Day
dialogue.text: Certainly. But the show has been moved to March 3rd. Your tickets are still valid.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, I'll be away then. I'd rather have my money back.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Day
dialogue.text: In that case, I can offer a refund minus the booking fee.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: But the cancellation wasn't my fault. Shouldn't I get the full amount?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Day
dialogue.text: You're right. Since the event was canceled, the booking fee is refunded too.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks. How long will it take?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Day
dialogue.text: About five working days. It'll go back to the card you paid with.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. Could I have a receipt for the refund?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Day
dialogue.text: Of course. Here it is, with your reference number.

titleEn: Choosing a school for a younger brother
titleTh: เลือกโรงเรียนให้น้องชาย
scenarioSentences: Your little brother starts high school next year.
Your parents must choose between two schools.
One is close, and the other has better results.
Dad wants your opinion.
You talk after dinner.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Dad, have you decided about Sam's school yet?

dialogue.speaker: Dad
dialogue.text: Not yet. The school across town has better results, but it's an hour by bus.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Two hours a day on a bus is a lot for a twelve-year-old.

dialogue.speaker: Dad
dialogue.text: True. But at the local school, he might not get into a good college.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. Results depend on the student, not just the school.

dialogue.speaker: Dad
dialogue.text: Maybe. Your mother thinks the local school has improved recently.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then why don't we visit both before deciding? Their open days are next month.

dialogue.speaker: Dad
dialogue.text: Good idea. And Sam should come too. It's his decision as well.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'll find the dates and put them on the calendar.

titleEn: Deciding how to spend prize money
titleTh: ตัดสินใจใช้เงินรางวัลของทีม
scenarioSentences: Your volleyball team won a local tournament.
The prize is eight hundred dollars.
Clara, the team captain, wants new uniforms.
Most players would prefer a team trip.
You discuss it with Clara after practice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Clara, about the prize money. Most of the team would rather go on a trip.

dialogue.speaker: Clara
dialogue.text: I know, but our uniforms are falling apart. We look terrible at games.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How much would new ones cost?

dialogue.speaker: Clara
dialogue.text: About four hundred for the whole team, including shorts.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So if we spent half on uniforms, we'd still have four hundred left.

dialogue.speaker: Clara
dialogue.text: That's not enough for a weekend away, though.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It is if we stay at the beach campsite and take the train.

dialogue.speaker: Clara
dialogue.text: That could work. As long as everyone agrees, let's split it fifty-fifty.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. I'll put it to a vote in the group chat tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Clara
dialogue.text: And I'll order the uniforms once the vote's done.

titleTh: ร้องเรียนร้านออนไลน์เรื่องนาฬิกาปลอม
scenarioSentences: You bought a watch from a website last week.
It arrived yesterday, but it looks fake.
The logo is crooked, and it feels cheap.
Mr. Nash runs the online shop.
You call him to complain.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Nash, my watch arrived yesterday, but I think it's fake.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Nash
dialogue.text: That's impossible. All our watches come directly from the factory.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The logo isn't straight, and the back is plastic, not metal.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Nash
dialogue.text: Hmm. The supplier must have sent the wrong batch. I can send you a replacement.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Honestly, I'd rather have a full refund. I wouldn't trust a replacement.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Nash
dialogue.text: Fair enough. But I'll need the watch back first to check it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Who pays for the postage? I don't think I should.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Nash
dialogue.text: You're right. Send it by any courier, and I'll add the postage to your refund.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And how soon would I get my money?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Nash
dialogue.text: Within three days of receiving it. You have my word.

titleTh: สอนงานเพื่อนร่วมงานคนใหม่
scenarioSentences: You work at a busy bakery.
Dev started his first week on Monday.
He keeps making mistakes at the cash register.
Your manager asked you to train him.
You talk to him after closing.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Dev, got a minute? I wanted to talk about the register.

dialogue.speaker: Dev
dialogue.text: I know, I gave the wrong change twice today. I'm really sorry.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Don't worry, everyone struggles at first. What's confusing you most?

dialogue.speaker: Dev
dialogue.text: The discount codes. There are so many, and customers get impatient when I'm slow.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Understandable. What if I wrote the main codes on a card by the register?

dialogue.speaker: Dev
dialogue.text: That would help a lot. I'd rather check a card than keep asking you.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And let's have a quick check-in after each shift this week.

dialogue.speaker: Dev
dialogue.text: Sure. Is it okay if I count the cash with you tonight, too?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good idea. If you practice that, you'll feel much more confident.
